:::{#exm-acceleration-factor}
#### Computing an acceleration factor

Suppose there is one covariate, with coefficient $\beta_1 = \logf{2}$,
and a subject has $x_1 = 2$.
Then:

$$
\ba
\hazfactor(\vx)
&= \expf{\eta(\vx)}
&& \text{(definition of the acceleration factor)} \\
&= \expf{\beta_1 x_1}
&& \text{(one covariate, no intercept)} \\
&= \expf{2 \logf{2}}
&& \text{(substitute } \beta_1 = \logf{2} \text{ and } x_1 = 2 \text{)} \\
&= 4
&& \text{(} \expf{\logf{a}} = a \text{, and } 2 \logf{2} = \logf{4} \text{)}
\ea
$$
:::
